question_text: A chronological singly linked transaction log stores old est entries at its head; an alternative stack stores new est entries at top. Outline two differences when inspecting recent transactions while preserving the log.
adaptation_rationale: Original application rewritten to be self-contained; assessed reasoning retained within cited 2027 scope.
solution: Stack gives direct access to the new est entry at its top.; The stated linkedlist must traverse from its old-entry head to reach recent entries.; Accessing entries below stack top normally requires pop ping newer entries.; Those popped entries must be restored correctly, whereas linkedlist traversal can read entries without relinking/removing them.
